summary: What did we develop?Our team of three created Astrocrates, an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical triage software that continuously tracks eight vital metrics: heart rate, HRV, spo2, body temperature, radiation exposure, sleep, exercise, and psychological mood. Powered by official NASA open data and spaceflight standards, our program validates incoming biometric streams, filters out sensor anomalies, and automatically ranks health risks by clinical urgency.How does it address the challenge?Astrocrates directly addresses the space mission health challenge by eliminating telemetry overload, cross-correlating multi-metric degradation against NASA benchmarks, and triggering automated escalation protocols when anomalies occur.Why is it important?During deep-space missions where communication delays with Earth prevent real-time monitoring, rapid intervention saves lives. Astrocrates ensures severely ill astronauts are immediately prioritized and observed by medical personnel as fast as possible.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?Astrocrates is an autonomous biometric telemetry, data-validation, and clinical triage system built by our team of three for deep-space missions. The software continuously ingests eight critical physiological and environmental metrics: heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), blood oxygen saturation SpO2, body temperature, radiation exposure, sleep duration, exercise load, and psychological mood. First, our backend validation layer checks incoming streams for sensor glitches, hardware dropouts, and impossible physiological spikes. Next, it evaluates validated data against official NASA spaceflight baselines (NASA-STD-3001, NASA OCHMO technical briefs, and NASA Human Research Program standard measures). When multi-metric deviations occur, Astrocrates classifies the severity into urgency tiers and triggers an automated escalation protocol—immediately alerting onboard crew and medical personnel to critical cases.

What benefits does it have? Eliminates Alert Fatigue: Filters out false positives and sensor noise so medical officers focus exclusively on genuine clinical risks. Holistic Health Visibility: Combines cardiovascular, respiratory, radiation, physical, and psychological indicators into a single unified dashboard rather than isolated data silos. Rapid Triage: Automatically ranks crewmembers by medical urgency, cutting down diagnostic time during high-stress emergencies.

What is the intended impact of the project? As human spaceflight advances toward Artemis lunar missions and Mars exploration, communication delays with Earth prevent real-time manual monitoring by Flight Surgeons. Astrocrates empowers crews with autonomous medical decision-support, ensuring that severely ill or rapidly deteriorating astronauts are identified and treated within critical golden-hour windows. Beyond spaceflight, this architecture can be adapted for remote Earth-based medicine, polar expeditions, and emergency disaster triage. What tools, coding languages, hardware, and software did we use? Languages & Frameworks: Python and C++ (telemetry processing, validation logic, and threshold scoring), Dart and Flutter (cross-platform clinical monitoring interface), and JavaScript (data visualization and integration scripts). Backend & Version Control: PocketBase (real-time database, authentication, and alert state storage), Git, and GitHub (collaborative version control). AI & Hardware: ChatGPT and Gemini (assisting with NASA documentation research, edge-case simulation design, and rapid prototyping) running on our team's personal laptops.

How is the project creative?Instead of treating astronaut vitals as isolated numbers with static alarms, Astrocrates applies a multi-factor clinical triage model inspired by space medicine. By cross-correlating physiological stress (HR, HRV, temperature, SpO2 alongside behavioral and environmental stressors (sleep debt, exercise load, mood, and cumulative radiation), the system distinguishes harmless physical exertion from genuine medical emergencies—turning raw spaceflight telemetry into an intuitive, prioritized medical dispatch workflow.What factors did your team consider?Scientific & NASA Alignment: Grounding all thresholds and safety ceilings directly in NASA-STD-3001 and NASA Human Research Program benchmarks rather than arbitrary cutoffs.Sensor Reliability: Designing sanity checks to handle noisy microgravity telemetry without missing acute emergencies (such as sudden radiation spikes or hypoxia).Human-Centered Usability: Building a clean, scannable Flutter UI that communicates urgency immediately to fatigued astronauts under high cognitive load.
